hints: Notice the drop is held stationary, so the upward electric force on charge $q$ must exactly balance the downward weight $mg$.
Recall the uniform field between the plates is $E = V/d$ with plate separation $d$ and p.d. $V$.
Set $qE = mg$, substitute $E = V/d$, then rearrange to isolate $q/m$.
walkthrough: Stationary means resultant force is zero, so upward electric force equals downward weight: $qE = mg$.
For parallel plates, the uniform electric field strength is $E = V/d$, where $V$ is in volts and $d$ is in $\text{m}$.
Substitute $E$ into the force balance: $q(V/d) = mg$.
Divide both sides by $m$ and multiply by $d/V$: $q/m = mgd/(mV) = gd/V$.
Check units: $gd/V$ has units of $\text{N C}^{-1}$ divided by $\text{N kg}^{-1}$ equivalent, giving $\text{C kg}^{-1}$ for $q/m$. This is option A

options.A: Balances weight $mg$ with electric force $qV/d$, giving $q/m = gd/V$.
options.B: This is the reciprocal $V/dg$, which equals $m/q$ not $q/m$.
options.C: This multiplies by $V$ instead of dividing, so it does not satisfy $mg = qV/d$.
options.D: This has $g$ in the denominator, so a larger $g$ would wrongly give a smaller $q/m$.
